article.articleHeadline: West Nile fever: What is known about the virus that killed a person in Brazil.

A probable case is in Piauí. The virus is maintained mainly in birds and transmitted by Culex mosquitoes; humans and horses are incidental dead-end hosts. About 80% of infections are asymptomatic; 20% develop fever, headache, body aches, and sometimes rash, often misdiagnosed as dengue. Less than 1% develop neuroinvasive disease (meningitis, encephalitis, poliomyelitis-like paralysis); about 10% of those die, with higher risk after age 70. - West Nile virus outbreak persists in Greece, with 75 new cases and 6 deaths reported in the past week by EODY, including a 13-year-old hospitalized patient. The virus has appeared in 35 municipalities in the Attica region. The project, started in winter, seeks to differentiate West Nile virus from other mosquito-borne viruses; clinical studies are planned. If successful, results are expected within about two years, with market release around 36 months. International partners include Italy, Spain, Estonia, the Netherlands, and Brazil, alongside Greece.

article.articleHeadline: Poultry farmers, stay vigilant during the monsoon; once these diseases spread, devastation begins.
article.articleSummary: During the monsoon in Gonda, India, poultry farming faces rapid spread of diseases unless cleanliness and vaccination are maintained. article.articleHeadline: Kolkata Doctors Treat Rare H1N1-Induced Acute Pancreatitis In 6-Year-Old Jharkhand Girl
article.articleSummary: Six-year-old girl from Jharkhand with influenza A(H1N1) infection developed rare extrapulmonary complications: acute pancreatitis and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS). After about two weeks of unresolved high fever in Jharkhand, she was transferred to Kolkata's Peerless Hospital on July 31 in critical condition with abdominal pain and mild respiratory distress. Laboratory and clinical assessment linked H1N1 to pancreatic inflammation and MAS, a dangerous hyperinflammatory state. Treatment included high-flow nasal cannula for five days, oral oseltamivir, high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin for two days, hydration, and early enteral feeding to prevent bacterial translocation. Fever resolved and inflammatory markers improved; after 12 days in the PICU she was discharged to return home to Jharkhand. This case underscores that influenza may cause rare complications like pancreatitis and MAS in children, beyond respiratory illness, in India.

article.articleHeadline: Mosquito bites are less frequent, but the West Nile virus is now spreading faster.
article.articleSummary: West Nile virus infections in Serbia total 11 laboratory-confirmed cases, with 10 neuroinvasive (meningitis or encephalitis), across Central Banat, South Banat, South Bačka, West Bačka, Šumadija District, and Belgrade. Average age is 66.2 years, highlighting higher risk among older and chronically ill individuals who require hospitalization. Risk peaks late August to early September; temperatures above 30°C speed viral replication in mosquitoes and shorten the incubation period from about three weeks at 20°C to 4–7 days. Domestic Culex pipiens and Asian tiger mosquitoes (Aedes albopictus) are moving into urban habitats, increasing bite exposure. Symptoms begin 3–14 days after bite; most infections are asymptomatic, about 20% have fever, headache, nausea/vomiting, and roughly 1 in 150 develop encephalitis or meningitis with potential lasting neurological effects. Dengue and chikungunya are not reported in Serbia; no imported/exported cases are described. EU totals exceed 600 cases in 10 countries, Italy and Greece most affected.

article.articleHeadline: Why India needs to look beyond typhoid to address the health burden of Salmonella infections
article.articleSummary: India faces a dual Salmonella burden: typhoid (S. Typhi) and non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS). A Lancet study (2023 data) estimates 4.9 million typhoid cases and about 7,850 deaths in India, with ~730,000 hospitalisations and fluoroquinolone resistance in 82% of those cases. Typhoid spreads via contaminated food and water; NTS causes gastroenteritis but can invade the bloodstream in children, the elderly, and immunocompromised. Outbreaks include an eggs-linked Salmonella outbreak sickening 98 people since November, reflecting a broader contamination chain from farms to kitchens. A One Health perspective is needed: safe water, sanitation, hygiene, and robust food safety in the informal sector. Antimicrobial resistance is rising: fluoroquinolone resistance among S. Typhi reached ~85% in 2015–19; ceftriaxone resistance observed in Thane (2025) outbreak (44/167). Carbapenem-resistant S. Typhi with blaNDM-5 reported. Blood culture remains the main diagnostic before antibiotics.

article.articleHeadline: New Dengue Antibody Cuts Viral Load in Indian Phase II Trial
article.articleSummary: Phase II trial of Dengue-mAb, a single-dose monoclonal antibody, conducted at 12 hospitals in India, shows rapid reduction in dengue viremia and faster fever clearance in adults aged 18–60 with fever onset within 48 hours. In 250 randomized participants (249 analyzed), dosing at 3,5,7, or 9 mg/kg IV vs placebo. At 24 hours, adjusted mean log reduction in viremia ranged 0.77–1.21 logs compared with placebo. Among the 32 participants with detectable viremia at baseline, 5,7,9 mg/kg groups cleared viremia by 8 hours, whereas placebo cleared by 72 hours. Fever clearance among baseline febrile patients occurred by median 3.5 hours (5 mg/kg) and 2.0 hours (7 mg/kg) versus 26.8 hours with placebo; 24‑hour fever clearance: 92.9% (3 mg/kg), 100% (5 & 7 mg/kg), 94.1% (9 mg/kg) vs 58.3% placebo. No treatment-related serious adverse events. Phase III planned; results apply to non-severe dengue in adults.

A total of 324 suspected cases have been reported; results for 314 of the 324 have been returned, with 42 positives. The case fatality proportion among confirmed patients is about 66.7%. Chandipura virus is an arbovirus transmitted by sandflies, causing acute encephalitis and disproportionately affecting children. The National Centre for Disease Control notes laboratory confirmation by quantitative PCR among methods. The outbreak follows monsoon-season surveillance, with cases reported from multiple districts rather than a single village. With 10 samples pending, figures may rise or fall as results come in. Previous outbreaks in Gujarat include 2024, when NCDC deployed a multidisciplinary team for surveillance and response.

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases are rising: Cancer specialist explains when flu symptoms should actually worry you, how to build resilience
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-28, H1N1 (swine flu) cases are rising. Cancer specialist Dr. Arpit Bansal notes that disease severity varies widely even within the same household, depending on health and immunity. He cautions not to panic but to heed warning signs and seek timely medical advice. Bansal advocates proactive health screening, citing vitamin D as a key factor; he routinely checks vitamin D levels before surgery, targeting 50–80 ng/mL, noting that many Indians are deficient. He also highlights gut health as central to immunity, recommending adequate fibre, fermented foods, a varied diet, about seven hours of sleep, and staying hydrated to support the body's flu response. The piece stresses resilience through prevention and timely care.

article.articleHeadline: Rescuing a pregnant woman with dengue fever and severe complications.
article.articleSummary: An obstetric dengue case in Ho Chi Minh City: a pregnant woman from Dong Nai at 39 weeks developed dengue in early August and underwent cesarean delivery. Postpartum hemorrhage, severe coagulopathy, fulminant hepatic failure, shock, and multi-organ failure followed. She was admitted to Gia Định People’s Hospital in a comatose state with hypotension and on mechanical ventilation; platelet count was 17 x 10^9/L. Multidisciplinary resuscitation included blood transfusion, respiratory support, plasma exchange, liver failure management and infection control. Due to extensive uterine damage and persistent bleeding, a hysterectomy was performed. Ongoing pelvic hemorrhage prompted angiography and embolization to stop bleeding, avoiding another major operation. After more than 15 days of therapy, she regained consciousness, breathes independently, and can eat and care for herself; the baby is stable. Doctor Trần Quang Huy notes this complex case highlights dengue’s critical phase in pregnancy and the need for vaccination and mosquito avoidance.

article.articleHeadline: Expert shares solutions to protect infants from the effects of RSV.
article.articleSummary: RSV remains a leading cause of hospitalization for bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants under 1 year in Vietnam, with severe cases requiring ICU care and mechanical ventilation. Infants’ immature immunity and small airways predispose to lower respiratory tract injury; more than 60% of ICU/ventilator RSV cases occur in otherwise healthy full-term infants. While some infections resolve spontaneously, many progress to hospitalization or death. Long-term effects may include recurrent wheeze and higher asthma risk before age 6. A Vietnamese RSV prevention symposium organized by the Vietnamese Pediatric Association in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, funded by Sanofi-Aventis Vietnam, drew nearly 1,000 healthcare workers. Strategies discussed include maternal vaccination and the monoclonal antibody Nirsevimab, approved by the Ministry of Health in 2025 for all children under 1 year. The association also released 'Nirsevimab in Clinical Practice—FAQs (2026)' for clinicians.

triage.notes: 本記事はRSV予防に関する医療従事者向けシンポジウムと新薬(Nirsevimab)の紹介であり、アウトブレイクや異常な感染増加の報告ではないため、対象国のイベントとしての発生とはみなさない。

article.articleHeadline: Busia heightens Ebola watch, warns against frequent travels
article.articleSummary: Kenya’s Busia County intensifies Ebola vigilance amid the DRC/Uganda Bundibugyo virus outbreak. No confirmed Ebola cases detected at Busia and Malaba border points, but authorities warn that heavy cross-border movement (2,500–3,000 trucks daily) raises importation risk. Since Aug 19, 2026, screening has reached 139,026 travellers at Busia OSBP and 74,833 at Malaba OSBP. Public awareness has been scaled up: 19,163 learners and school communities; 15,921 market/public-place visitors; 3,672 church congregants; 248 baraza attendees; 6,107 vulnerable individuals received Ebola prevention messages. Seven suspected cases in Matayos and one each in Teso Central and Butula subcounties tested negative. Port Health at Malaba emphasizes travel restriction to Ebola-affected areas, particularly DRC. Health officials continue border surveillance and community outreach to prevent introduction of Ebola while promoting hygiene, early reporting, and cautious travel.

triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニア・ブシア県における国境監視強化であり、ケニア国内での確定エボラ例は報告されていない（疑い例はすべて陰性）。実際のアウトブレイク発生地はDRC/ウガンダだが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCのみをverified_locationsとした。

article.articleHeadline: US issues guidance on travellers denied boarding a flight over Ebola-related restrictions
article.articleSummary: Ebola-related flight restrictions tied to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) outbreak are in effect. Anyone physically present in the DRC within 21 days of a scheduled US-bound flight is barred from boarding, regardless of citizenship. In addition, foreign nationals and US lawful permanent residents who have been in Uganda or South Sudan are barred from US flights until 21 days after leaving those countries. Travellers who have been in Uganda or South Sudan but not the DRC may fly to the United States, but must enter through Washington Dulles, Atlanta, Houston, or New York's JFK. Affected travellers should email Ebola-Travel-HELP@hq.dhs.gov with full name, date of birth, passport details, current location, and flight information; automated replies may occur, followed by a response by phone or a verified .gov address. For emergency lodging or consular services, contact the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria outbreak kills two workers at Germany's busiest airport -- RT World News
article.articleSummary: Two Frankfurt Airport workers have died in a rare malaria outbreak linked to Anopheles mosquitoes apparently imported by plane from a malaria-endemic country. The outbreak began in early July 2026; the first death occurred shortly afterward, with diagnosis confirmed posthumously. The Robert Koch Institute (RKI) confirmed four cases among airport employees in mid-July; local media later reported a total of six male workers infected, mostly handling luggage. Frankfurt health authorities say the population risk remains very low and malaria is not transmitted person-to-person, only by mosquitoes. Authorities captured several mosquitoes at the airport and sent them for genetic analysis to determine origin; the outbreak is an example of "airport malaria," a phenomenon last seen at Frankfurt in 2023. Malaria symptoms include fever, chills, headaches, and fatigue; severe cases can cause organ failure. Global malaria deaths were about 610,000 in 2024, with most deaths in Nigeria, DRC, Niger.

article.articleHeadline: Deforestation, the gold rush, and the return of Ebola - Olivier Monod
article.articleSummary: Seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared May 15, 2026, spread faster than all outbreaks; as of August 25, there are over 5,656 cases and 2,715 confirmed deaths. The epidemic began in Mongbwalu, Ituri province, in the northeast, a region identified by risk maps as high for Ebola resurgence. Deforestation, mining and population movements linked to informal gold mining near Mongbwalu drive increased human–virus contact. Around a dozen gold mines encircle Mongbwalu; forest clearance facilitates exposure by bats and other wildlife, with direct or indirect spillover via hunted animals. A 2024/2025 assessment by Carson Telford and colleagues linked deforestation, climatic factors and hunting to Ebola emergence; satellite data show 15% forest loss in the region over 25 years, with accelerating deforestation in the last 15 years (Global Forest Watch, IPIS). Surveillance gaps persist: more than 80% of new cases occur outside known contact lists, hindering containment.

triage.headline_ja: 森林破壊、ゴールドラッシュ、そしてエボラの再来 - オリヴィエ・モノー
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生中の第17回エボラ流行が過去最速の拡大を見せ、死者2,715人・症例5,656人超に達しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 致死率約48%と非常に高く、新規症例の80%以上が既知の接触者リスト外で発生しているため、サーベイランスと接触者追跡に重大なギャップがある。森林破壊・非公式金鉱採掘による人獣接触増加が流行拡大の要因とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Kwango: Drinking water, a solution to permanently eliminate cholera in Popokabaka (zone medical officer) - ACP
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in Popokabaka Health Zone, Kwango, Democratic Republic of Congo, is being contained largely through safe drinking water. Dr. Alain Mboko, zone medical chief, says eliminating cholera requires providing potable water, noting the epidemic stems from use of unsafe water due to the absence of a clean-water production unit. He appeals to the central government, provincial authorities, and international partners to rehabilitate the water production point that formerly served Popokabaka. MSF support has improved patient management and community education, with local staff trained for structured care. Since the outset, 864 patients have been treated in Popokabaka, with cure rate about 97% and case-fatality down from 18.7% in June (week 27) to 2%. Innocent Burundi of MSF describes faults at the Nkoti river intake—deviation, sand in the decanter, and a corroded galvanized steel main—recommending polyethylene piping, cleaning intake boxes, and protection; work will take time but will restore water access.

triage.headline_ja: クワンゴ州:飲料水がポポカバカのコレラを根絶する解決策(ゾーン医療責任者)-ACP

triage.notes: コレラはDRCで地域流行性の疾患であり、本記事はポポカバカ保健ゾーンでの既存流行の管理状況（MSF支援、致死率改善）と水インフラ復旧の必要性を報じるもの。新規・異常な発生ではないが、清潔な水供給の欠如という構造的問題が続く限り再流行リスクがあり、国際支援（中央政府・州当局・国際パートナーへの訴え）が明示的に要請されている。

article.articleHeadline: Pinga Health Zone: after two postponements, the vaccination campaign against polio, measles, and rubella finally launched.
article.articleSummary: Polio, measles, and rubella vaccination campaign launched on 27 August 2026 in Pinga Health Zone, Walikale Territory, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, after two postponements due to logistical constraints. Vaccination supplies, previously blocked at Walikale-centre, arrived in Pinga, enabling the campaign. Interim Health Zone Chief Dr Théophile Muka notes that more than 45,000 children aged 0–14 are targeted. Over five days, vaccination teams will operate to protect children against these three vaccine-preventable diseases. Dr Muka appeals to parents and guardians to seize the opportunity and have their children vaccinated. The campaign occurs amid ongoing health-service access challenges in Walikale, driven by difficulties in delivering medical products and inputs.

triage.headline_ja: ピンガ保健地域:2回の延期を経て、ポリオ・麻疹・風疹予防接種キャンペーンがついに開始

triage.notes: 記事は実際の症例報告ではなく、物流上の問題で2度延期された予防接種キャンペーンの開始を報じるもの。北キブ州ワリカレ地域は紛争等によりアクセスが困難な地域であり、45,000人以上の児童が対象。ワクチン未接種児童の蓄積による将来的なアウトブレイクリスクの観点から経過観察が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Bunia University shifts to videoconferencing to limit transmissions - ACP
article.articleSummary: During an Ebola outbreak in Ituri's Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Bunia University (UNIBU) suspended in-person lectures for cohorts larger than 50 students and shifted to videoconferencing to limit close contacts and reduce transmission risk on campus. Rector Prof. Jean-Faustin Simba announced the measure on 27 August 2026. The policy affects faculties with high student populations; practical instruction for medical students is suspended due to heightened exposure in health facilities. A parallel training program, developed with the outbreak response team, will prepare future physicians to resume clinical rotations with appropriate knowledge and personal protective equipment kits. The university emphasizes protecting students and staff while awaiting strengthened capacities in the surrounding health system. No casualty figures are provided in the report.

article.articleHeadline: Uasin Gishu strengthens Ebola preparedness amid high population movement
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-27, Uasin Gishu County conducted a training for health workers to strengthen preparedness against possible Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreaks. The exercise covers surveillance, infection prevention and control, case investigation, and coordination, with emphasis on swift, coordinated response. Public Health Emergency Operations Center Manager Jude Oduor highlighted the Incident Management System (IMS) for coordinating Ebola readiness, calling for clearly defined roles and effective communication to ensure suspected cases are identified, reported and managed promptly to prevent transmission. Officials noted Uasin Gishu's strategic position and high mobility: Eldoret hosts health facilities and serves as hub; the county's petroleum hub and Eldoret Central Market link to North Rift and to the Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing movement of patients, traders, and transporters. This mobility underscores the need for robust surveillance, early detection, and rapid response to minimize Ebola importation. The exercise is part of capacity-building for public health emergencies.

triage.triage_reason: 実際のエボラ発生や疑い症例の報告はなく、ケニア・ウアシンギシュ州における予防的な準備訓練の実施に関する記事であるため、シグナルとしての対象外と判断する。

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: In the shadow of Ebola, the surge in cholera cases worries the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Cholera in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) eclipses the Ebola response with about 39,500 suspected cases and 1,173 deaths in 2026 (weeks 1–32), CFR 2.97%. Endemic provinces—North Kivu, South Kivu, Tanganyika, Haut-Katanga, Haut-Lomami—now report spread to non-endemic areas, where mortality is more than sixfold higher. In the week of Aug 3–9, 2026, 1,528 suspected cases and 29 deaths occurred across 70 health zones in 16 of 26 provinces. Over the last four weeks, non-endemic areas account for 2,012 cases and 162 deaths (CFR 8.05%), versus endemic areas with 3,442 cases and 45 deaths (CFR 1.31%). CFR is highest among children under 5 in non-endemic zones (8.49%). Hotspots include Sud-Kivu and Nord-Kivu; transmission also in Kwango, Mai-Ndombe, Sud-Ubangi, and Équateur. Re-emergence in Isangi (Tshopo) and Nyunzu (Tanganyika). Stockouts of Ringer’s lactate and rapid tests; fragile treatment centers, including a deteriorating center in Lubumbashi. OMS priorities: functional treatment facilities, enhanced surveillance, supply chains, water chlorination, disinfecting, and community outreach; conflict further hampers response.

article.articleHeadline: Kinshasa: Dog vaccination, a necessity to prevent transmissible diseases (a veterinarian) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On Aug 27, 2026, Kinshasa veterinarians urged dog vaccination as essential to prevent transmissible diseases between dogs and humans during World Dog Day, celebrated Aug 26 annually. Dr. Alain Furaha, head of the Rabies Vaccination and Control Office (OVCR), emphasized rabies vaccination as critical given its high fatality in humans once symptoms appear. The WHO cites dog vaccination as a key strategy to interrupt rabies transmission at its source. Vaccination programs should cover all pets in Kinshasa, with age-tailored schedules and a regular deworming cadence—no more than three months between dewormings in DRC. Beyond vaccines, he stressed animal and environmental hygiene, including daily cleaning of the dog's feeding bowl. He warned about dog meat consumption risks and advised veterinary health checks before consumption. The OVCR oversees vaccination status, legalization/registration of vaccines in Kinshasa, and handling dog bite cases citywide.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Lubero: Maximum Vigilance Recommended for the Inhabitants of the Bamate Chiefdom - ACP
article.articleSummary: On Aug 27, 2026, in Lubero, the Bamate Chiefdom in North Kivu, DRC, Mwami Shabani Mukosasenge urged maximum vigilance amid an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain. Since the outbreak declaration on May 15, 2026, the DRC had over 5,600 confirmed cases and more than 2,700 deaths as of Aug 25. The Bamate authority warns the disease is extremely dangerous and can kill rapidly if not treated promptly. Residents are urged to report any symptoms compatible with Ebola to health services, avoid physical contact with patients or the deceased, and never handle or wash a corpse under suspicious circumstances. Emphasis on strict preventive measures: regular handwashing, avoid contact with body fluids, use protection when caring for the sick, and cooperate with health teams. Community involvement is essential to containment and decision-making.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in an era of budget cuts, by Marta Ricart.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaches 100 days with 5,600 cases and 2,700 deaths; Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths, apparently controlled. Case fatality rate about 47%. WHO says the epidemic is still growing in DRC. Some 16,000 vaccines have arrived, with 70,000 planned, mainly for health workers, though effectiveness against this strain is uncertain. By comparison, the 2018 outbreak took 235 days to reach 1,000 infections; this year 1,000 cases occurred in 40 days. Mortality is seven times higher than the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (>11,000 deaths). Analysts attribute rapid spread to reduced international aid after the U.S. withdrew from the WHO and cut contributions; the U.S. has spent over $500 million on the response and imposes a travel rule: anyone who has been in DRC in the last 21 days cannot fly to the U.S. until another 21 days outside Congo. Security and access challenges limit detection (about 40%); calls for stronger regional health investments persist (WHO, UN, MSF, Africa CDC).

triage.headline_ja: 予算削減時代のエボラ出血熱、マルタ・リカルト

article.articleHeadline: 'Behind every case, a person': the man leading DRC's Ebola fight on the human cost hidden behind the numbers
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo variant Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has 5,656 confirmed cases and 2,715 deaths as of 24 August, the largest and deadliest outbreak since 1976 and the 17th in the DRC; outbreak first declared in May. Prof. Pierre Akilimali, head of the National Public Health Institute and incident manager for a multi-agency response, emphasizes that behind every case is a person and a family, while acknowledging cases may rise as community engagement improves and treatment centres adapt. Cross-border risk involves Uganda, which has recently declared itself Ebola-free after several border cases. The eastern DRC’s war-weary, distrustful context includes attacks on clinics, complicating response. The effort calls for regional and international solidarity, with concerns about funds channeled through NGOs and delayed wages; authorities insist responses must strengthen, not collapse, the broader health system and maintain access to care for other conditions.

triage.headline_ja: 「一人一人の症例の背後に、人がいる」：数字の裏に隠れた人的被害と向き合うDRCのエボラ対策責任者
triage.triage_reason: 1976年以来最大かつ最も死者数の多いエボラ流行（コンゴ民主共和国、確定5,656例・死亡2,715例）であり、越境（ウガンダ）リスクや治療センターへの攻撃など地域不安要素もあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, fifty years on: the story of an epidemic that repeats itself.
article.articleSummary: Current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, has reached 5,677 cases and 2,717 deaths as of 24 August 2026, the second-largest Ebola outbreak by case count and the largest in the DRC. A New England Journal of Medicine commentary uses half a century of foci to highlight persistent gaps in epidemic preparedness. It recalls 1976 dual outbreaks—in Yambuku, DRC (Zaire ebolavirus) and Nzara, Sudan (Sudan ebolavirus)—where a 44-year-old teacher sparked nosocomial transmission, yielding 318 cases and 280 deaths (88% CFR). The piece contrasts with the 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak (>28,000 cases, >11,000 deaths) and exports to the US and Italy, which prompted WHO to declare a PHEIC in August 2014. The authors stress frontline health workers and communities, and note legacies such as Africa CDC (2017).

triage.notes: 記事はNEJMの解説記事で、1976年のヤンブク（DRC）とンザラ（スーダン）の初発事例、2013-2016年の西アフリカ流行（米国・イタリアへの輸出例含む）を歴史的に振り返る内容。ウガンダも現行流行の発生地とされているが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には記載せず。現行流行の規模（5,677例、2,717死亡）は重大であり、続報の詳細確認とフルRRAが推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Porto Velho conducts more than 26,000 malaria tests in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil, recorded 2,499 confirmed malaria cases from January 1 to August 17, 2026, up 8% from the same period in 2025. A total of 26,335 tests were performed: 22,615 thick-smear exams and 3,720 rapid tests. Of the confirmed cases, 2,293 were Plasmodium vivax, 188 Plasmodium falciparum, and 18 were mixed infections. Diagnosis and treatment are provided free by the public health system (SUS). Testing is available at Prontos Atendimentos, UPAs, labs, and basic health units across urban, rural, and district areas of Porto Velho. Health authorities emphasize surveillance, active case finding, vector control, and rapid treatment initiation. Symptoms include high fever, chills, headache, body pains, nausea, and vomiting, especially after exposure in forested areas, near rivers, or recreational sites. Prevention focuses on repellents, protective clothing, screens, bed nets, and access for health teams to perform mosquito-control measures.

article.articleHeadline: Ceará confirms fifth Mpox case in 2026; state records 65 notifications this year.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) in Ceará, Brazil, reached five confirmed cases in 2026, with 65 notifications reported this year. The most recent diagnosis was on July 23, 2026, per an update released on July 26. The patient is a man aged 30–39; health authorities continue epidemiological surveillance in Ceará via the IntegraSUS platform. Year-to-date, there are 65 notifications, 5 confirmed, 60 discarded, and no cases under investigation. The first confirmed case of 2026 was announced on March 10 through the CNIEV (National Center for Epidemiological Intelligence and Genomic Surveillance) dashboard, with records showing the first three infections contracted in February and the fourth in March. Despite ongoing new cases, the majority of notifications have been discarded, and authorities maintain permanent monitoring of the situation.

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis: Health Data Reveal a Warning That Requires Action Before Diagnosis.
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis B remains a pressing public health issue in Rondônia, Brazil, where 2025 data show 406 new HBV cases and a rate of 23.2 per 100,000—well above the national average (5.2) and second only to Acre. Hepatitis C accounted for 201 cases (11.5/100,000), with Porto Velho among capitals with higher incidence. The report links current transmission to Amazonian sanitation history, vertical transmission, and older medical practices, noting many patients were likely infected decades ago. Yet prevention and care are within reach: rapid tests at Basic Health Units yield results in about 15 minutes; the hepatitis B vaccine is free for all ages; medicines are available through SUS. In 2025, 16 HBV cases were reported among pregnant women (0.7 per 1,000 live births; national 0.3), underscoring the need for prenatal testing and vaccination. Actions: expand active case finding, testing, vaccination, prenatal care, and continuous treatment.

article.articleHeadline: Daily Mail: Europe faces an epidemic of 'rain rot' transmitted sexually.
article.articleSummary: Rain rot (Dermatophilus congolensis), historically an animal disease, has caused human infections across several European countries, with cases in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Spain, and others by mid-2026. The outbreak features human-to-human transmission via close contact, as some patients had no livestock exposure. Skin lesions present as rashes, pustules, and crusting, potentially in the groin, face, trunk, and limbs. Most cases respond to antibiotics and rarely result in severe outcomes. Experts caution that shifting transmission pathways may be driving the rise; clinicians should consider rain rot in patients with unusual dermal lesions. Overall population risk remains low, but cross-country surveillance continues. Separately, in mid-August 2025, three UK residents were diagnosed with Oropouche virus, known as ‘sloth fever,’ a tropical disease usually found in Brazil, underscoring concurrent tropical disease concerns.

article.articleHeadline: Feevale hosts the 1st Congress of Animal Virology and Infectious Diseases - O Sul Newspaper
article.articleSummary: Feevale hosts the first Congress of Animal Virology and Infectious Diseases on September 11–12, 2026, at the Salão de Atos, Campus II, Novo Hamburgo, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. Registration is free at feev.as/108d6f1, with a donation of 1 kg of animal feed requested to emphasize the event's community focus. article.articleHeadline: Newcastle disease in birds on two Azores islands.
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease virus detected in wild birds on the Azores' Graciosa and Terceira islands, with laboratory confirmation as of 26 August 2026. Wild-bird mortality had been reported on Graciosa, Terceira, Pico, São Miguel, Santa Maria, and Faial, but current testing confirms the virus only on Graciosa and Terceira. Affected species are rock pigeons and turtle doves; other Faial samples tested negative to date. The disease poses a low risk to humans but warrants precautions. Following detection, the Azores regional government banned pigeon hunting and bird fairs; the ban on hunting the rock pigeon took effect on the subsequent Friday and remains in place indefinitely across all islands. No human cases reported, and no infection source or imported/exported cases are described.

article.articleHeadline: Fight against dengue gets a boost with the installation of the EDLs.
article.articleSummary: Sixty Estações Disseminadoras de Larvicida (EDLs) are being installed in Lucas do Rio Verde, Mato Grosso, Brazil to combat Aedes aegypti. Initial deployment targets high-risk sites such as tire shops and scrap yards, designated as Strategic Points due to dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya risk. Each unit holds water and a larvicide-treated screen; the female mosquito spreads the chemical to other breeding sites, inhibiting egg development. The city was chosen based on ovitrampa data identifying hotspots. Last health bulletin (2–8 August) records 1,288 notifications this year, with 249 confirmed dengue and 132 pending results. A citywide cleanup has been under way since 7 August in Jardim Primaveras, Rio Verde, Veneza and Vida Nova, with plans to move to Fujii, Américas, Araras and Amazônia. Authorities emphasize community participation and care for the devices.

article.articleHeadline: Genomic analysis of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto: genetic diversity and population structure
article.articleSummary: Genomic analysis of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto characterizes genetic diversity and population structure of the parasite. The work leverages genomic data to assess diversity across global populations. A multinational collaboration includes institutions in Australia, Estonia, China, Italy, Chile, Iran, Spain, Türkiye, Algeria, Brazil, Argentina, Armenia, Saudi Arabia, Slovakia, and other countries, reflecting broad geographic sampling. By focusing on genetic diversity and population structure within E. granulosus sensu stricto, the study provides baseline insight into geographic patterns of variation in this parasite and informs understanding of its evolutionary dynamics. The affiliations span Melbourne, Tartu, Shenzhen, Rome, Valdivia, Tehran, Isfahan, Gorgan, Madrid, Elazig, Algiers, Santa Maria, Neuquén, Yerevan, and more. Published 2026-08-27.

article.articleSummary: {"description":"Sporotrichosis surges in Londrina, Brazil, with cases more than doubling versus 2025. The fungal infection can spread from animals to humans. article.articleHeadline: CRDT has prepared infrastructure for safe care of infectious and contagious diseases - Diário do Amapá
article.articleSummary: CRDT in Macapá, Amapá, Brazil, has prepared infrastructure for safe care of infectious and contagious diseases, prioritizing airborne pathogens such as tuberculosis and Hansen’s disease (leprosy). It uses separated workflows, dedicated air-conditioned consultation rooms, and respiratory protection with ventilation-focused strategies to reduce airborne particle exposure. The center provides infectious diseases, pneumology, and dermatology services, serving about 250–300 patients daily within the SUS framework to deliver specialized care near home. Access begins with clinical evaluation; suspected TB or Hansen’s disease patients are routed to CRDT after a general clinician assessment. Dermatology and pneumology appointments are scheduled via Super Fácil, while infectious disease care can be accessed directly. Hours are Monday–Friday, 8:00–17:00, at Rua Professor Tostes, Santa Rita, Macapá. Users must present SUS Card, personal documents, and any required referral.

article.articleHeadline: Dourados confirms 7 cases of chikungunya in one week.
article.articleSummary: As of August 27, 2026, Dourados, Brazil, reports seven new chikungunya confirmations in the 32nd epidemiological week (Aug 16–22), bringing the cumulative totals to 5,180 confirmed cases, 44 suspected, 5,197 discarded, and 47 awaiting classification. In the Indigenous Reserve, 3,190 notifications yield 2,314 confirmed cases. The outbreak has caused 18 deaths overall, including 11 Indigenous residents from the Bororó and Jaguapiru villages. The week 12 peak recorded 1,209 notifications and 672 confirmed. The city remains in a public health emergency; vector-control efforts by endemic agents—house-to-house visits, notifications, and fines—have contributed to a decline in cases. Authorities urge continued vigilance: eliminate standing water inside homes, keep backyards clean, and avoid improper waste disposal to prevent further transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Daycare center suspends classes after confirmation of a case of scabies.
article.articleSummary: Daycare center in Ibatiba, in the Caparaó region of Brazil, suspended classes after a confirmed case of scabies in a student. The infection was identified in one classroom, and the school promptly implemented measures to prevent transmission, notifying the Municipal Sanitation Surveillance, which advised on necessary precautions. As a preventive step, the facility will undergo cleaning and pest-control treatment over the weekend, with activities expected to resume on Monday, August 31. The Education Department stated that all feasible measures have been taken to reduce transmission and that the situation is being monitored. Scabies is a skin disease caused by a small mite; transmission occurs mainly through direct, prolonged contact with an infected person, particularly in close-contact settings. Symptoms include intense itching at night and skin lesions; the disease is treatable and controllable with appropriate measures.

article.articleHeadline: Health expands list of countries that require yellow fever vaccination for travelers from Costa Rica.
article.articleSummary: Beginning August 31, Costa Rica’s Ministry of Health expands the list of countries for which Costa Rican citizens and residents traveling abroad must show yellow fever vaccination. The new additions are Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana. The vaccination requirement remains for travelers to Colombia, Brazil, Peru, and African destinations under national health regulations. Christian Valverde, Director General of Health, announced the update. Yellow fever is a viral disease transmitted primarily by mosquito bites. Health officials urged travelers to verify destination entry requirements in advance and complete vaccination in a timely manner to avoid entry issues.

article.articleHeadline: Alagoas, Mato Grosso and Roraima are on alert for an increase in Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome.
article.articleSummary: Alagoas, Mato Grosso, and Roraima are on alert for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) with rising activity, Fiocruz Infogripe bulletin 2026-08-27 reports. In Mato Grosso and Roraima, increases are mainly in 2–4-year-olds; in Alagoas, 2–14-year-olds. The causative virus is not yet identified; rhinovirus (common cold) is suspected to drive most pediatric cases, with metapneumovirus contributing less. Seasonal influenza A has ended; severe influenza A cases are low, with a slight rise in influenza B in Bahia and Mato Grosso. Four capitals - Aracaju, Belém, Boa Vista, João Pessoa - show long-term SRAG growth. Eight states - Amazonas, Mato Grosso do Sul, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, Santa Catarina, Sergipe - are at alert/risk/high risk without clear growth. Findings show 100% success in coordinated care and viral eradication when linked to care, and both current inmates and new admissions benefit from one-off universal screening. Telemedicine is identified as an economical, scalable option to improve specialist access in prisons.

article.articleHeadline: Scientists Warn That a New Coronavirus Affecting Humans May Emerge from Cambodia Soon!
article.articleSummary: Cambodian bats in Steung Treng province yielded four sarbecovirus groups with potential to cross species barriers. From Aug 2020 to Jun 2023, researchers collected samples from 1,462 bats across nine genera; 146 samples tested positive for at least one coronavirus. Genetic analyses produced 33 complete genomes of previously uncharacterized sarbecoviruses. Recombination was frequent, and Cambodian viruses showed evolutionary links to viruses detected in Vietnam and Thailand, indicating regional movement beyond borders. Notably, spike proteins from groups 2 and 3 had receptor-binding domains with up to 96.8% amino-acid identity to SARS-CoV-2, and pseudovirus experiments demonstrated entry into cells via human ACE2 for a representative group-2 spike. However, isolated viruses were not recovered, so there is no evidence of current human infection or human-to-human spread. Notably, viruses lacked the SARS-CoV-2 polybasic furin cleavage site. Surveillance remains important given high diversity and recombination. The findings were published in Nature Communications.

article.articleHeadline: An 8-year-old girl dies after playing in a lake... 'brain-eating amoeba' fear.
article.articleSummary: An eight-year-old girl, Lilian Smart, died in Louisiana from Naegleria fowleri infection contracted while swimming in Claybon Lake. She developed fever, was hospitalized, and sustained severe brain damage, dying about eight days after onset. Naegleria fowleri causes Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis; infection occurs when warm freshwater enters the nasal passages, reaching the brain via the olfactory nerve. There is no transmission through drinking water and no human-to-human spread. From 1937–2025, roughly 180 US cases have been confirmed, with a case fatality around 97%. Prevention emphasizes avoiding swimming in warm lakes, rivers, and reservoirs during hot weather, not submerging the head, using nose clips, and ensuring well-maintained, chlorinated pools. For nasal exposure, boiled and cooled water or sterile saline should be used. Warming waters may expand the amoeba’s habitat northward; Korea reported one imported case in 2022 (a stay in Thailand), and cases have occurred in Japan and Taiwan.

article.articleHeadline: Complex interactions between ecological and host factors drive continental patterns of avian influenza outbreak risk in Eurasia and Africa
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza viruses (AIV) outbreaks across Eurasia and Africa from 2004–2025, exceeding 50,000 reports, were analyzed to reveal continental patterns and cross-subset differences among highly pathogenic (HPAI), low-pathogenic (LPAI), domestic, and wild-bird groups. Using a multi-algorithm machine learning framework with 27 ecological features, the study achieved predictive accuracies ≥84% and found strong non-linear, strata-specific risk drivers. For all-AIV and wild-bird cohorts, vegetation indices and wetland proximity were the top spatial predictors. In contrast, domestic duck and chicken densities dominated predictions for LPAI and domestic poultry subsystems, while proximity to LPAI outbreaks was the strongest driver of HPAI risk. Underreporting in wildlife and developing regions limits data quality, but the framework offers a flexible tool for risk-based surveillance and targeted interventions at regional and global scales.

article.articleHeadline: Hantavirus infects wildlife farmers in Vietnam: A risk to Southeast Asia
article.articleSummary: Vietnam wildlife farming (6,744 farms, 1.8 million animals across 371 species by 2021) poses hantavirus spillover risk. Infections may stem from exposure to infected wild rodents outside farms; transmission is via inhalation of dust contaminated with urine, droppings, or saliva. The findings underscore Southeast Asia risk, including Indonesia, and the need for genetic confirmation (RT-PCR/sequencing) and strengthened surveillance. Preventive actions include protective equipment, One Health collaboration, and stricter wildlife farming enforcement. In 2025, Andes hantavirus caused a shipborne outbreak on MV Hondius in South America: 13 infections and 3 deaths, likely started ashore with onward person-to-person spread.

article.articleHeadline: AI reads X-ray images to detect TB before it's too late.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia accounts for about 10% of global tuberculosis (TB) cases in 2024, second to India, with WHO estimating ~1.09 million Indonesians with TB in 2023 and an incidence of 387–388 per 100,000. In Jakarta, TBScreen.AI, a computer-aided detection system for chest X-rays developed by Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) and partners, screens for TB by highlighting radiographic shadows to prioritize further testing; it is not a diagnosis. In August 2026, TBScreen.AI showed sensitivity ~83% and specificity ~87%, promising for screening but requiring external multisite validation before wide-scale use. Prison settings illustrate active-case finding challenges: 2023 saw 6,039 TB diagnoses via screening; 2024 detection fell with symptom-based screening; 2025, broader X-ray screening identified 7,972 cases. Yearly case counts reflect screening coverage and methods, not direct incidence shifts, underscoring the need to translate detection into diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of transmission.

Central Luzon reported 16,057 cases; NCR 10,611; Calabarzon 10,320. Thirteen areas breached the epidemic threshold Jul 5 - Aug 1 (Mandaluyong, Lapu-Lapu, Zamboanga; Abra, Agusan del Sur, Albay, Aurora, Camarines Norte, Davao Oriental, La Union, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Zamboanga Sibugay); Cebu, Mandaue, and Davao de Oro breached the alert threshold. Takeda's Qdenga (TAK-003) is under review in the Philippines; WHO prequalified and approved in 40+ countries; two doses 3 months apart; recommended for children 6-16 in high-transmission settings. Regulators note lower efficacy in ages 4-5 and potential serotype 3 risk in dengue-naïve recipients. Dengue remains endemic; Gloriani urges vaccination alongside prevention.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱死者300人超、専門家がワクチン使用を強く推奨
triage.triage_reason: 全国的には症例数は減少傾向だが、13地域で流行閾値を超え死者300人超と重症度が高く、ワクチン導入をめぐる政府・専門家の関心も高いためフルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: フィリピンで毎年発生する季節性デング熱の年次報告記事。全国的には前年比で症例数・死者数ともに減少しているが、13地域で epidemic threshold を超過し地域的な深刻さが継続している。Takeda社ワクチン(Qdenga)の承認審議が進行中で、政策的関心が高い点が特徴。

article.articleHeadline: Quezon logs 2,276 cases, 12 deaths from January to August
article.articleSummary: Quezon province, Philippines, reported 2,276 dengue cases and 12 deaths from January to August 22 this year, a 38% reduction versus 2025, according to the Quezon Provincial Health Office. Of the 2,276 cases, 1,018 were suspected, 467 probable, and 791 confirmed dengue infections. Mauban municipality recorded the highest burden with 406 cases and four deaths. Children aged 1 to 10 accounted for 38% of total cases, and 46% showed warning signs of severe dengue. Dengue is transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes; common symptoms include high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pains, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and skin rashes. Severe dengue can cause persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, and breathing difficulties. Authorities stress early diagnosis and prompt treatment to prevent severe complications and deaths.

triage.triage_reason: デング熱は毎年季節的に発生する地域流行性疾患であり、症例数・死亡数は前年より減少傾向にあるため緊急のフルRRAは不要だが、小児への影響や重症化率がやや高いため経過観察の対象とする。

article.articleHeadline: Suspected cases of foot-and-mouth disease in Al-A'sa.
article.articleSummary: Suspected foot-and-mouth disease among sheep in the Al-A’sa border area with Tunisia. The Western Plain veterinary police branch conducted a field visit, collected samples, and sent them for laboratory testing, while implementing biosecurity measures in the affected pens. Official data show 20 outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease across Libya, with spread into western and southern regions; the eastern region reports foci in six municipalities: Benghazi, Qaminis, Suluk, Tukrah, Marj, and Al Bayda. Hatim Al-Maslati, head of the National Center for Veterinary Health Surveillance and Rapid Response, says reports are rising but the disease remains under control and not at epidemic level, urging breeders and traders to strictly follow biosecurity. The first cases were reported on May 5, 2026 in Tajoura; since then further cases have appeared in Tajoura, Ain Zara, Misrata, Msallata, and Zawiya, with ongoing sampling and routine spraying/disinfection of affected stalls.

article.articleHeadline: Cebu City steps up meat checks, ASF controls
article.articleSummary: Cebu City intensified meat-safety enforcement and African swine fever (ASF) controls in July 2026. The Department of Veterinary Medicine and Fisheries condemned 1,151.75 kg and confiscated 711.755 kg of meat and animal products for violations (ante-mortem 593 kg, post-mortem 558.75 kg). Inspections covered 11,371 hogs and 139,209 chickens; two citation tickets and three warnings issued. Fish and marine products inspections totaled about 2.2 million kg with 73,374 containers, and 254,435.5 kg were re-inspected, monitoring 137 fish vendors; regulatory fees amounted to about P146,748. Total July collections reached about P2.45 million, with January–July 2026 at about P16.83 million (P107,050 in licensing, P31,000 in penalties). ASF-border controls were coordinated with the Bureau of Animal Industry Quarantine Office 7 and Cebu Port Authority; biosecurity campaigns and intensified vaccination were conducted in barangays including Inayawan, Quiot, Cogon Pardo and adjacent rural areas. Rabies-control vaccinations totaled 2,184 in July, with vaccination and welfare activities ongoing across the city.

article.articleHeadline: Cebu dengue cases rise to 2,324 as PHO steps up community prevention drive | Carmel Pedroza
article.articleSummary: Within Jan 1–Aug 18, 2026, Cebu Province, Philippines, reports 2,324 dengue cases and 17 dengue-related deaths. The Cebu Provincial Health Office (PHO) is intensifying community-driven prevention to eliminate mosquito-breeding sites amid rising cases since July; the rainy season is blamed for more stagnant water, though breeding can occur in clean water in vases, gutters, and storage containers. Dengue response was activated in July; local government units, barangays, and households are urged to perform cleanup; dengue brigades are in place, with expanded emphasis in schools. Highest case counts are in Talisay City (272), Toledo City (217), and Medellin (182), with the provincial government offering assistance. Cleanup remains the primary intervention; misting is a last-resort measure after breeding sites are removed. Parents are urged to bring feverish children to RHUs or hospitals; tests are available at RHUs and 16 government hospitals for fever 3–5 days.

triage.triage_reason: フィリピン・セブ州における季節性デング熱の増加で、死亡例もあるが例年発生する地域的流行であり、異常性・国際的拡大の懸念は低い。継続的な監視が妥当。
triage.notes: デング熱はフィリピンで毎年雨季に発生する疾患であり、地方自治体レベルの予防活動が既に実施されている。全国的・国際的な緊急性は低いが、死亡例が続いている点は経過観察が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Leptospirosis cases in Baguio down 39 percent; 1 confirmed dead
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis in Baguio City, Philippines, reached 14 confirmed cases from Jan 1 to Aug 15, 2026 (per Aug. 25 CESU statement), down from 23 in the prior year, with 1 laboratory-confirmed death: a male farmer who died June 14. Three other deaths occurred among suspected cases (two: construction worker and delivery rider, both died in June and tested negative; one student who died this month awaiting results). Of the 14 confirmed cases, 13 are male (about 92–93%) aged 24–71. Cases were reported across barangays Irisan, Camp 7, Bakakeng Central, Phil-Am Compound, Quirino-Magsaysay, Middle Quezon Hill, Outlook Drive, Happy Hollow, City Camp Proper and Kias. High-risk groups include farmers, construction workers, delivery riders, painters, animal caretakers, welders and other outdoor workers exposed to water or soil contaminated with rodent droppings; symptoms include fever 3–5 days, severe headache and reddened eyes, with jaundice possible in severe cases. Public health measures: education, rodent control, drainage clearing, PPE promotion with delivery hubs and construction sites; medicines available for treatment.

article.articleHeadline: High leptospirosis cases among children 'alarming' -- Manila hospital doctor
article.articleSummary: Manila's Ospital ng Maynila Medical Center reports a leptospirosis surge with nine pediatric and eleven adult cases in the emergency department as of Thursday evening, prompting conversion of vacant upstairs rooms into dedicated leptospirosis wards. Hospital director Dr. Reynaldo Salinel Jr. and Manila Mayor Isko Moreno redirected resources amid overwhelmed facilities, with a surge linked to flooding around August 17 and expectations of more arrivals due to ongoing heavy rains. Symptoms include fever, headache, and muscle pain; progression to Weil's disease can involve the lungs, brain, kidneys, and liver. Medicines are restocked; staffing will be augmented with job-order personnel for information dissemination. Public guidance emphasizes avoiding floodwaters, boiling drinking water, wearing boots, maintaining hygiene, and flu vaccination to reduce illness risk.

triage.notes: 洪水を契機とした季節性のレプトスピラ症流行であり、ヒト-ヒト感染はなく国際的拡大リスクは低いが、マニラ市内の医療体制への負荷と続報の必要性からピックアップ対象とした。

article.articleHeadline: Medical Shortages, Monsoon Illnesses Put More Than 600 IDPs at Risk in Western Pai Khun - Shan Herald Agency for News
article.articleSummary: More than 600 internally displaced people (IDPs) in Lar Tein Village, western Pai Khun (Pekhon) Township, face a healthcare crisis as seasonal flu and fevers spread during the monsoon, amid a regime blockade on medical supplies. Displaced from Baw Yan, Taung Hsa Long and Myauk Hsa Long villages since September 2025, they have endured nearly 11 months of displacement. Remote, mountainous terrain and damaged roads hinder transport of medicines, and regime restrictions on basic goods worsen shortages. Local resistance medics provide care but cannot meet demand. Medicines are urgently needed, especially for flu and malaria. Across western Pai Khun, more than 6,000 people from about 10 villages remain displaced, sheltering in forests and host communities with little access to humanitarian assistance.

triage.triage_reason: ミャンマー西パイクンの国内避難民（600人以上）で季節性インフルエンザとマラリアが拡大し医療アクセスが不足しているが、症例数・死亡者数など具体的な深刻度データが不明であり、国際的拡大リスクも低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は人道支援・医療アクセス問題が主題であり、感染症アウトブレイクとしての具体的な症例数・重症度・死亡者数の情報が欠落している。軍政による医療物資封鎖が状況を悪化させているが、これは公衆衛生緊急事態というより人道危機の側面が強い。

article.articleHeadline: Two Airport Workers Die Of Malaria In Frankfurt, Germany, After Mosquito Stows Away On Aircraft
article.articleSummary: Two Frankfurt Airport workers have died of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Germany, linked to an Anopheles mosquito that stowed away on an aircraft. The four workers fell ill between July 4–6, and authorities identify an imported, aircraft-transported mosquito as the most likely source; all involved had no recent travel to malaria-endemic areas. This remains a rare instance of “airport malaria” in non-endemic settings. Malaria can be deadly if untreated, and early symptoms (fever, headache, chills) can delay diagnosis when travel history is absent. The public risk is deemed very low; blood analyses are underway to determine whether one or multiple bites occurred. Past Frankfurt cases (2022–2023) and a 2024 Eurosurveillance study suggesting Ghana as a parasite origin emphasize imported disease risks. Globally, malaria kills hundreds of thousands annually, but is preventable and curable with rapid treatment.

triage.triage_reason: 発生国はドイツ（対象国外）であり、ガーナは寄生虫起源に関する過去研究として言及されているのみで実際の発生地ではないため、対象地域における監視シグナルとしては該当しない。
triage.notes: 本事例は「空港マラリア」と呼ばれる稀な現象で、輸入蚊によるヒト-ヒト感染の可能性はなく、公衆衛生上のリスクは非常に低いとされている。ガーナは2024年の研究で寄生虫の起源として言及されているのみで、発生国はドイツであり対象国リストに含まれないため、地域監視の観点からは見送りとする。

article.articleHeadline: Rabies claims five lives in the Western and Western North regions
article.articleSummary: Five people have died of rabies in Ghana's Western and Western North regions in 2026, with August 27 reporting fatalities across Wassa East (2), Jomoro (1), Amenfi East (1), and a Diaso case linked to Bibiani in the Central Region. A suspected rabid stray dog in a Sekondi suburb attacked nine people, including children. Vaccination coverage in the two regions stands below five per cent, far below the 70 per cent threshold needed to interrupt transmission; the combined dog/cat population is about 166,000. Between 2015–2021, dog-bite rates averaged roughly 78 per 100,000 in Western and 73 per 100,000 in Western North. Kola nuts are not a cure. Donor support for vaccination drives is urgently needed; authorities urge dog vaccination, registration, and stricter controls on stray and free-roaming dogs to prevent further deaths.

triage.headline_ja: 西部・西部北部地域で狂犬病により5人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病による複数死亡と予防接種率の著しい低さ（5%未満）が報告され、当局が国際的な支援（ドナー支援）を求めていることから、WPRO基準複数該当かつ社会的・政治的関心が確認されるためフルRRAへの移行を推奨。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はガーナで既知の流行病であり国際的拡大リスクは低いが、予防接種率の著しい低さと死亡者数増加、ドナー支援要請という点でローカルな公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。続報でワクチン接種状況・症例数の推移を確認する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: Oti Region records four Mpox cases; all patients recover
article.articleSummary: Mpox in Oti Region, Ghana: four confirmed mpox cases in the first half of 2026, with all patients fully recovered after treatment. Suspected Cerebrospinal Meningitis cases were negative on laboratory tests. Dr Kofi Amo-Kodieh, Oti Regional Director of Health Services, announced at the 2026 Mid-Year Performance Review in Worawora, Biakoye District. Early detection, prompt treatment and robust disease surveillance underpinned the favorable outcome. Authorities call for sustained surveillance, community reporting, and continued public education on prevention and prompt care. Efforts to strengthen disease surveillance, laboratory testing and response mechanisms will continue, with emphasis on adequate resources, logistics and personnel to support hard-to-reach communities and guide the second half of 2026 toward timely, equitable healthcare.
